> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR

> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f8bcc4009746af392fdf55d5ca1e66179c6d3f22` — the merge of head `c7102b32fe4ee4d880635a3ac9d95b34aa79f4f5` into base `6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f8bcc4009746af392fdf55d5ca1e66179c6d3f22 && git checkout f8bcc4009746af392fdf55d5ca1e66179c6d3f22
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2 c7102b32fe4ee4d880635a3ac9d95b34aa79f4f5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2 && git merge --no-ff c7102b32fe4ee4d880635a3ac9d95b34aa79f4f5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #24924 · `domain:services` seat 2 · `os-support-ai` · `session_01UmqzD97e14iws6hmVhgZ5y` · 2026-10-20T20:56Z · head `c7102b32fe`. This follows patch round 1 (the seat's correction and REWORK `6300407976` on the card); it is the review of record for claim `6298731457`. Contract review: not owed. The PR touches no published schema and no governed path, and it now declares `Clause-②: no` with no narrowing arm, so none of the four contract faces is hit.

1. **Form:**
   - The first line is `Fixes #24924`. The seat's grep of the body finds no other closing keyword beside an issue number.
   - `Clause-②: no` is at line start in the body and in the `service-messaging` changeset (`patch`), with its one-line reason: nothing a write could send before is refused.
   - 10 files, +350/−33.
   - Path face, read with the files endpoint on this head: `check-governed-merges --pr 24976` reports not governed, 383 changed lines. Ordinary queue landing.
2. **Premise and fix:**
   - The ruling record `6293376907` governs: no stored-row conversion carries the narrowing, so 18.x warns on write and corrects the copy. The dev measured that no ADR-0087 conversion carries data rows of a platform object.
   - `channel_renders_template` is a `format` rule at `severity: 'warning'`. Its pattern is built from `TEMPLATE_CHANNELS` (`email`, `sms`). A write naming another channel is accepted and stored, and it reports one advisory: `rule`, `severity: 'warning'`, `field: 'channel'`, `code: 'invalid_format'`, and a message that points in-app content to an email template.
   - Read on the diff: nothing refuses. The pin's refusal-word grep hits only docblock prose.
   - **Pins:** 15 real-engine cases (ObjectQL with SqlDriver over better-sqlite3).
     - Nine warning cases, each asserting the write accepted, the row stored, and exactly one advisory.
     - Three silence cases.
     - Three stored-row preservation cases.
   - **Ablations:**
     - Rule inert: the 9 warning cases red, `expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`.
     - Inverse, the rule warns on everything: the 3 silence cases red.
     - Both restored to the HEAD blob `84c52411f6b9`.
3. **Gates:**
   - CI on `c7102b32fe`, latest run per check name: 42 checks, 34 success, 8 skipped, 0 failed.
   - Every skip is on the roster in `scripts/pm/check-expected-skips.mjs` (read from the file): Auto Label, Check PR Size, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, the 18.x upgrade harness and Packed-tarball smoke.
   - Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are both `success`.
   - Check Changeset's first run was red because it read the body's stale `(narrowing)` line. Its re-run after the seat applied the body edit is `success` (run `118880480939`).
   - Local: 98 derived, 98 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. `service-messaging` typecheck exits 0; its suite runs 54 files, 608 passed. plugin-auth's two phone-SMS files pass (7 tests).
4. **Accepted deviations:**
   - The copy does not say that a named email template is used "on every channel", as the dispatch asked. That is false for SMS, so the shipped copy states the measured behaviour.
   - The subject help also dropped "inbox title".
   - An inverse ablation was added.
   - The PR-body edit was handed to the seat, and the seat applied it.
   - Prose read sentence by sentence against the diff and the cited code:
     - In the changeset, the two readers of a row, the accepted-and-stored write, which answers carry `warnings` and that bulk and import only log it, and the unchanged stored rows.
     - In `authentication.mdx`, no shipped row, and the read in `tenancy.defaultOrgId()`: the Default Organization's row under `single`, the built-in text under `isolated` and `group` (as PR #24930 made it).
5. **Out of scope:**
   - The SMS channel ignores a notify `template`: carried by #24770, with a note posted there (`6301298178`). No reach was measured, so it was not filed.
   - Bulk updates and import commits answer the advisory only in the server log: Acceptance notes, carrier none (an existing surface's coverage, no surface added).
   - objectui `SelectField` clears an out-of-set stored value on load (source reading): carried by the 19.0 refusal card the seat files when this lands, because it decides that card's spelling.
6. **Landing:** ordinary queue landing. Every check on this head is green or an expected skip, so the seat flips it (`pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`) on this record. After the merge, the seat files the 19.0 refusal card. #24923 (same package's translation bundles) is next in line behind this PR.
